Treatment summary
Patient presented following a collision sustained while the patient's vehicle was struck during a left-hand turn. The
reported mechanism is consistent with the shoulder injury diagnosed, and the force described fits the pattern of soft
tissue damage seen in this type of impact. Over eleven visits, care included physical therapy, range-of-motion work,
and home exercise instruction. Recovery ran somewhat longer than typically expected for this injury, which we
attribute to the patient's pace of progress rather than any single setback. On examination, certain findings, including
reduced active abduction and tenderness over the rotator cuff insertion, support the clinical diagnosis. Other tests,
such as neurological screening and stability assessment, returned normal results. The patient reports a minor strain
to the same region many years ago, which resolved completely without ongoing limitation and does not appear to
affect the current presentation. Billing records reviewed for this episode show no repeated charges for the same
services.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
